question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The philanthropist's __________ donations significantly improved the quality of life in the community.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. substantial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence says the donations "significantly improved the quality of life", so a positive, large-quantity word is needed. "Substantial" means large in amount, size or importance; considerable. (पर्याप्त / बड़ी मात्रा में)

◦ Correct: The philanthropist's substantial donations significantly improved the quality of life in the community.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "meagre" means very small/inadequate — the opposite of what improved life significantly.

• Option 3 "parsimonious" means stingy/mean with money.

• Option 4 "redundant" means unnecessary or no longer needed.

NOTE

• Synonyms of substantial: considerable, sizeable, ample, significant. Antonyms: meagre, scanty, insignificant, negligible.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Faithfull.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Faithfull" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "faithful" — the suffix "-ful" is always written with a single "l" when added to a word. (सही वर्तनी — faithful)

◦ Correct: faithful (meaning loyal, true, reliable). (वफ़ादार)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Peaceful", "Lovable" and "Joyful" are all correctly spelt.

• Note: the suffix is "-ful" (full of), not "-full": careful, useful, beautiful, wonderful, faithful.

NOTE

• When the standalone word "full" becomes a suffix, it drops one "l": hope + ful = hopeful; faith + ful = faithful. But as an adverb it takes "-fully" (faithfully).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is ___________ of spiders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. afraid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "afraid" takes the preposition "of" — "afraid of (something)" means frightened/scared of it. (से डरना)

◦ Correct: She is afraid of spiders.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "interest" and Option 3 "fear" are nouns/verbs, not adjectives, and do not fit after "is ___ of".

• Option 4 "frightening" means "causing fear" (active) — "She is frightening" would mean she scares others, changing the meaning.

NOTE

• Adjective + preposition collocations: afraid of, fond of, proud of, aware of, scared of, jealous of, capable of. "Afraid of + noun/gerund" (afraid of the dark / afraid of failing).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Dig up dirt
option_1: To uncover negative information about someone or something.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To uncover negative information about someone or something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "dig up dirt (on someone)" means to discover and reveal damaging/negative or scandalous information about a person or thing, usually to harm their reputation. (किसी की बुराई/कमज़ोरी खोद निकालना)

◦ Example: The reporters tried to dig up dirt on the politician before the election.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "find and disclose evidence" is too neutral/general and misses the negative, scandalous sense.

• Options 3 and 4 are unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Here "dirt" is used figuratively to mean damaging gossip or scandal, not literal soil. Similar: "dish the dirt" (gossip about someone).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Following weeks of intense training, the athlete ____________________ in the championship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. competed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Following weeks of intense training" refers to a completed action in the past (a single event at the championship), so the simple past tense "competed" is correct.

◦ Correct: Following weeks of intense training, the athlete competed in the championship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "were competing" is plural ("were"), but the subject "the athlete" is singular.

• Options 2 and 4 (present perfect / present perfect continuous) do not suit a finished past event described with "following weeks of training".

NOTE

• Simple past = V2, used for a completed action at a definite past time (competed, trained, won). Subject–verb agreement: a singular subject ("the athlete") takes a singular verb form.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Obedence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obedence" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "obedience" (note the "i": obed-i-ence), meaning the act of obeying; compliance with orders/rules. (आज्ञाकारिता)

◦ Spelling key: O + BE + DI + ENCE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Aggravate" (to make worse), "Fabulous" (wonderful) and "Tremendous" (very great) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related forms: obey (verb), obedient (adjective), obedience (noun). Both the adjective and noun keep the "i": obedient, obedience.

question:
Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.

These are the works of a great poet Tagore.
option_1: These are the works of that great poet Tagore.
option_2: These are the works of an great poet Tagore.
option_3: These are the works of this great poet Tagore.
option_4: These are the works of the great poet Tagore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. These are the works of the great poet Tagore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When we speak of a particular, well-known/specific person ("the great poet Tagore"), the definite article "the" is used, not the indefinite "a".

◦ Correct: These are the works of the great poet Tagore.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "an great" is wrong — "an" is used only before a vowel sound, and here we would need "the" anyway.

• Options 1 "that" and 3 "this" are demonstratives that wrongly add a pointing sense not required here.

NOTE

• Use "the" before a noun made specific/unique (the sun, the great poet Tagore, the Ganga). "A/an" is for a non-specific, singular countable noun mentioned for the first time.

question:
Select the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence.

The state played only a modest part in the outstanding advancement of modern morality.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Boastful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "modest" means humble, unassuming, not boastful; small in size or amount. Its antonym is "boastful" (proud of oneself and eager to tell others; showing off). (विनम्र का विलोम — घमंडी/डींग मारने वाला)

◦ Example: The modest scientist never bragged, unlike his boastful rival.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Unimpressive" and Option 3 "Moderate" are close in sense to modest (not opposite).

• Option 4 "Humble" is a synonym of modest, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of modest: humble, unassuming, unpretentious, moderate. Antonyms: boastful, arrogant, conceited, immodest, showy.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the incorrectly spelt word in the given sentence.

She is an indepandent writer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Independent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "indepandent" should be spelt "independent", meaning free from outside control; self-reliant; not depending on others. (स्वतंत्र)

◦ Correct: She is an independent writer.

• Spelling key: IN + DE + PEN + DENT (all three vowels after "d" are "e").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The distractors are all wrong spellings: "Indipendant", "Indipendent" and "Independant" incorrectly use "i" or "a" where "e" is required.

NOTE

• Remember: independent and dependent both end in "-ent" (adjectives). The noun form is "independence / dependence".

question:
Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the given idiom.

When pigs fly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Just impossible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "when pigs fly" is used to say that something will never happen; it is impossible. (जब सूअर उड़ेंगे — यानी कभी नहीं / असंभव)

◦ Example: "He'll clean his room when pigs fly" — meaning he will never do it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options (in unity, in due course of time, correct approach) do not convey the sense of impossibility.

NOTE

• Similar idioms meaning "never/impossible": "once in a blue moon" (very rarely), "till the cows come home" (for a very long time), "not in a million years".

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.

While learning to drive, Shivani met with an accident because she couldn't hit the _________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. brake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "brake" is the device used to slow down or stop a vehicle. In the context of driving and an accident, she couldn't hit the brake. (ब्रेक — वाहन रोकने वाला उपकरण)

◦ Correct: ... she couldn't hit the brake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Break" (a homophone) is a verb/noun meaning to shatter or a pause/interval — not the vehicle part.

• "Brick" (a building block) and "brack" (not a standard English word) do not fit.

NOTE

• Homophones = words that sound alike but differ in meaning/spelling: brake / break, brake (stop a car) vs break (shatter / a rest). Other pairs: their/there, principal/principle, stationary/stationery.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined word.

"He was notorious for his avaricious behaviour, always seeking ways to accumulate more wealth."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. greedy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "avaricious" means extremely greedy for wealth or material gain. Its one-word substitute is "greedy". The clue "always seeking ways to accumulate more wealth" confirms this. (लोभी / लालची)

◦ Example: His avaricious/greedy nature made him hoard money endlessly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "notorious" means famous for something bad (already in the sentence, not the underlined word's meaning).

• Option 3 "sloth" means laziness.

• Option 4 "generous" (giving freely) is the opposite of avaricious.

NOTE

• Synonyms of avaricious: greedy, grasping, covetous, money-grubbing, rapacious. Antonym: generous. (Related noun: avarice = extreme greed.)

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The residents of Rameswaram / about the 1940s were quite / orthodox, but were also / tolerant of other communities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. about the 1940s were quite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To refer to an approximate period of time, the correct preposition is "around" (or "in"), not "about". So the segment should read "around the 1940s".

◦ Correct: The residents of Rameswaram around the 1940s were quite orthodox, but were also tolerant of other communities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "The residents of Rameswaram", "orthodox, but were also" and "tolerant of other communities" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• "About" usually means "concerning/approximately with numbers" (about 50 people), while "around" is preferred for approximate time periods/dates (around the 1940s, around noon).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We are planning to see an _________________ perform a symphony.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. orchestra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "symphony" is a long musical composition played by an "orchestra" — a large group of musicians playing various instruments together. So one goes to see an orchestra perform a symphony. (वाद्यवृंद / ऑर्केस्ट्रा)

◦ Correct: We are planning to see an orchestra perform a symphony.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "opera" is a drama set to music (with singing), not the group that performs a symphony.

• Options 3 "actor" and 4 "actress" perform in plays/films, not symphonies.

NOTE

• The article "an" before the blank signals a word beginning with a vowel sound — "an orchestra" fits perfectly. A symphony is typically in four movements, performed by an orchestra.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The cat likes to _________ in the sun during the afternoon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. lie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lie" (lie – lay – lain) is an intransitive verb meaning to rest/recline in a flat position and takes no object. The cat likes to lie (rest) in the sun. (लेटना)

◦ Correct: The cat likes to lie in the sun during the afternoon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Lay" (lay – laid – laid) is transitive and needs an object ("lay the book on the table"); it does not fit here.

• "Lye" is a strong alkaline chemical; "lei" is a Hawaiian flower garland — both are unrelated nouns.

NOTE

• Common confusion: lie (to recline, no object: I lie down) vs lay (to put something down, needs object: I lay the pen down). Present tense here needs "lie".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The movie was so boring that I fell _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. asleep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression "fall asleep" means to start sleeping. After the verb "fell", the adjective "asleep" is required. (सो जाना)

◦ Correct: The movie was so boring that I fell asleep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "fell slept" / "fell sleep" / "fell sleeping" are all grammatically incorrect — "fall" is followed by the adjective "asleep", not a verb form.

NOTE

• "Asleep" is a predicative adjective used after linking/"fall" type verbs (fall asleep, be asleep). We do not usually place it before a noun (we say "a sleeping child", not "an asleep child").

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

After months of / meticulous planning and hard work, / a team successfully launched / their innovative product to the market.
option_1: their innovative product to the market.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a team successfully launched.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The later pronoun "their" refers back to a specific, already-identified team, so the definite article "the" should be used, not the indefinite "a". It should be "the team successfully launched".

◦ Correct: After months of meticulous planning and hard work, the team successfully launched their innovative product to the market.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other segments ("After months of", "meticulous planning and hard work,", "their innovative product to the market.") are all correct.

NOTE

• Use "the" for a noun that is definite/known from context (especially when a possessive like "their" later refers to it). "A team ... their product" creates a mismatch between the indefinite and the definite reference.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Dr. Oppenheimer is the exceptional movie of all the movies in recent times.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the exceptional movie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "of all the movies" signals a comparison among many, which requires the superlative degree. So "the exceptional movie" should be "the most exceptional movie".

◦ Correct: Dr. Oppenheimer is the most exceptional movie of all the movies in recent times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Dr. Oppenheimer is", "of all the movies" and "in recent times" are all correct.

• The structure "the + superlative ... of all ..." (the most exceptional of all the movies) is the standard pattern.

NOTE

• Long adjectives form the superlative with "the most" (the most exceptional, the most beautiful). A superlative is used when comparing three or more things or picking one out of a whole group.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Cacophony
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Harmony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cacophony" means a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds; unpleasant noise. Its antonym is "harmony", meaning a pleasing, tuneful combination of sounds / agreement. (कर्कश ध्वनि का विलोम — सुरमयता/सामंजस्य)

◦ Example: The cacophony of the traffic gave way to the harmony of the orchestra.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Discord", 2 "Noise" and 3 "Dissonance" are all synonyms of cacophony (unpleasant/clashing sound).

NOTE

• Synonyms of cacophony: discord, dissonance, din, racket, clamour. Antonyms: harmony, euphony, melody, concord.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: A salesman insisted that the payment against an purchase should be done by using the bank card.
option_2: The salesman insisted that the payment against the purchase should be done by using a bank card.
option_3: The salesman insisted that a payment against the purchase should be done by using an bank card.
option_4: A salesman insisted that a payment against a purchase should be done by using a bank card.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The salesman insisted that the payment against the purchase should be done by using a bank card.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Option 2 uses the articles correctly: "the salesman", "the payment against the purchase" (specific, known items) and "a bank card" (any one card — correct because "bank" begins with a consonant sound).

◦ Correct: The salesman insisted that the payment against the purchase should be done by using a bank card.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses "an purchase" (should be "a purchase" — consonant sound).

• Option 3 wrongly uses "an bank card" (should be "a bank card").

• Options 1 and 4 misuse the indefinite "a salesman"/"a payment" where a specific "the" is meant.

NOTE

• Article rule for a/an: choose by sound, not spelling — "a bank card / a purchase" (consonant sound), "an apple / an hour" (vowel sound). Use "the" for specific, previously identified nouns.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. This gives Annapurna a (4)______ of 32%, making it the most statistically dangerous of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks. It is an avalanche-prone area with some technical difficulty. Climbers’ misery is (5)_______ by insufficient local support, in addition to unpredictable weather and inaccessibility.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. highest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mountains/peaks are ranked by their height, so "the world's ninth highest peak" is the correct and standard expression. Nanga Parbat is indeed the world's ninth highest mountain. (नौवीं सबसे ऊँची चोटी)

◦ Correct: ... Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth highest peak, competes with K2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "deepest" applies to oceans/valleys, Option 2 "lengthiest" to length, and Option 4 "fattest" to thickness — none describes a mountain's rank.

NOTE

• Peaks are measured by height/altitude. Mount Everest is the highest (8,849 m); K2 is second; Nanga Parbat is the ninth highest 8,000-metre peak.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. This gives Annapurna a (4)______ of 32%, making it the most statistically dangerous of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks. It is an avalanche-prone area with some technical difficulty. Climbers’ misery is (5)_______ by insufficient local support, in addition to unpredictable weather and inaccessibility.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ascent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ascent" means the act of climbing or moving upward, especially up a mountain. "The first ascent to the summit follows a narrow ridge" is the correct mountaineering expression. (आरोहण / चढ़ाई)

◦ Correct: The first ascent to the summit follows a narrow ridge.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rise" is more general (an increase); Option 3 "lift" and Option 4 "launch" do not describe climbing a mountain to a summit.

NOTE

• "Ascent" (going up) vs "descent" (going down). In mountaineering, "the first ascent" of a peak refers to the first successful climb to its summit.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. This gives Annapurna a (4)______ of 32%, making it the most statistically dangerous of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks. It is an avalanche-prone area with some technical difficulty. Climbers’ misery is (5)_______ by insufficient local support, in addition to unpredictable weather and inaccessibility.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. translates.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Translates (as)" means to give the equivalent meaning in another language. "Nanga Parbat", which translates as 'naked mountain', correctly explains the meaning of the name. (अनुवाद होता है / अर्थ होता है)

◦ Correct: ... the Nanga Parbat, which translates as 'naked mountain', 'Killer Mountain'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "transliterates" means to write in the letters of another script (not to give meaning).

• Option 2 "transposed" (to change position/order) and Option 4 "transcribes" (to write out/copy speech) do not convey "means in another language".

NOTE

• "Translate" (meaning across languages) vs "transliterate" (letters/script across languages, e.g., writing नमस्ते as "namaste"). Here the sense is the meaning, so "translates".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. This gives Annapurna a (4)______ of 32%, making it the most statistically dangerous of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks. It is an avalanche-prone area with some technical difficulty. Climbers’ misery is (5)_______ by insufficient local support, in addition to unpredictable weather and inaccessibility.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fatality rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage talks about the mountain being dangerous and deadly ("most statistically dangerous ... Killer Mountain"). A "fatality rate" of 32% means the percentage of deaths among those who attempt it. (मृत्यु दर)

◦ Correct: This gives Annapurna a fatality rate of 32% ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "economic rate" is irrelevant here.

• Option 2 "frailty rate" and Option 4 "mortal rate" are not standard collocations; the correct term for deaths is "fatality rate" (or "mortality rate").

NOTE

• "Fatality" = a death caused by an accident, disaster or disease. "Fatality rate / mortality rate" expresses deaths as a proportion of a group.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. This gives Annapurna a (4)______ of 32%, making it the most statistically dangerous of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks. It is an avalanche-prone area with some technical difficulty. Climbers’ misery is (5)_______ by insufficient local support, in addition to unpredictable weather and inaccessibility.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. exacerbated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exacerbated" means made worse or more severe. The climbers' misery is exacerbated (worsened) by insufficient local support, bad weather and inaccessibility. The passive structure "is exacerbated by" needs a past participle. (और बढ़ा दिया जाना / बदतर बनाना)

◦ Correct: Climbers' misery is exacerbated by insufficient local support ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "perfectly" and Option 2 "increasingly" are adverbs and cannot follow "is ___ by" in this passive construction.

• Option 4 "worst" is a superlative adjective, not a verb, so it is grammatically wrong here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of exacerbate: aggravate, worsen, intensify, compound. Antonyms: alleviate, ease, mitigate, relieve.

question: Which is the jet stream that brings Western disturbances in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Westerly jet stream.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Western Disturbances are brought to India by the subtropical Westerly jet stream. These are extratropical storms originating in the Mediterranean/Caspian Sea region and carried eastward by the westerlies. (पश्चिमी विक्षोभ — पछुआ जेट धारा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Western Disturbances bring winter rainfall to the north-western plains (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, western UP) and snowfall to the Himalayas.

• This winter rain (mahawat) is very beneficial for rabi crops, especially wheat.

NOTE

• A jet stream is a narrow band of very fast winds high in the atmosphere. The subtropical westerly jet stream also influences the onset/withdrawal of the Indian monsoon.

question: Aparna Satheesan, a recipient of 2021 Abhinandan Saroja National award by National Institute of Classical Dance, is an exponent of ________ and Kuchipudi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aparna Satheesan, a recipient of the 2021 Abhinandan Saroja National Award, is an exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi. (भरतनाट्यम और कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India/UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: According to Census of India 2011, which pair of states recorded the highest population density (persons/km2) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar and West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, among the states, Bihar (1,106 persons/km²) had the highest population density, followed by West Bengal (1,028 persons/km²). (बिहार और पश्चिम बंगाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Among Union Territories, Delhi had the highest density (about 11,320 persons/km²).

• Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest population density (17 persons/km²) among the states.

NOTE

• Population density = total population / total area (persons per km²). India's overall density as per Census 2011 was 382 persons/km².

question: Identify the place where the West Central Railway Zone headquarters is located.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jabalpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The headquarters of the West Central Railway (WCR) zone is located at Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh). (पश्चिम मध्य रेलवे — जबलपुर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The West Central Railway was formed in 2003 and has divisions at Jabalpur, Bhopal and Kota.

• Indian Railways is divided into zones, each headed by a General Manager.

NOTE

• Some zonal HQs: Central Railway – Mumbai; Northern – New Delhi; Western – Mumbai; Southern – Chennai; Eastern – Kolkata; North Central – Prayagraj.

question: Which of the following Rashtrakuta rulers performed the ceremony called ‘Hiranya Garbha’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dantidurga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rashtrakuta ruler Dantidurga (the founder of the dynasty) performed the ritual known as "Hiranya-garbha" (the golden-womb ceremony), a symbolic rite of rebirth to elevate one's status. (दंतिदुर्ग — हिरण्यगर्भ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the 8th century CE, with its capital at Manyakheta (Malkhed).

• The famous Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

NOTE

• The Hiranyagarbha ceremony was performed by the priests to grant kshatriya (royal) status. It is mentioned in relation to legitimising kingship.

question: Who can exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes in Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Speaker of Lok Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha can exercise a casting vote in the case of a tie (equality of votes). Normally the Speaker does not vote, but in a tie he/she casts the deciding vote. (लोकसभा अध्यक्ष — निर्णायक मत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This power is provided under Article 100 of the Constitution.

• In the Rajya Sabha, the Vice President (ex-officio Chairman) exercises the casting vote in a tie.

NOTE

• The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members; the first Speaker of independent India was G. V. Mavalankar. The Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill.

question: The autobiography of Sam Pitroda is called:
option_2: Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India" is the autobiography of Sam Pitroda (Satyanarayan Gangaram Pitroda), the telecom pioneer often called the "Father of India's telecom/IT revolution". (सैम पित्रोदा की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sam Pitroda played a key role in the C-DOT (Centre for Development of Telematics) and the spread of PCOs/STD booths in India in the 1980s.

• He headed the National Knowledge Commission.

NOTE

• "In the Afternoon of Time" is by Harivansh Rai Bachchan; "The Substance and the Shadow" is Dilip Kumar's autobiography; "Beyond the Lines" is Kuldip Nayar's autobiography.

question: On which of the following dates did the British Empire transfer its powers to the Constituent Assembly in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15th August.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 15th August 1947, the British Empire transferred its powers to the Constituent Assembly of India, and India became independent. (15 अगस्त 1947)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Indian Independence Act 1947 provided for the partition of British India into the two dominions of India and Pakistan and the transfer of power.

• The Constituent Assembly (formed in 1946) became the sovereign law-making body; Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister.

NOTE

• Key dates: 26 January 1950 – Constitution came into force (Republic Day); 26 November 1949 – Constitution adopted; 15 August 1947 – Independence Day.

question: The Right to Freedom of Religion is covered under which Articles of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 25-28.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Right to Freedom of Religion is guaranteed under Articles 25 to 28 of the Constitution of India. (धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 25-28)

◦ Article 25 – Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

◦ Article 26 – Freedom to manage religious affairs.

◦ Article 27 – Freedom from taxes for promotion of a particular religion.

◦ Article 28 – Freedom from religious instruction in State-funded institutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• These form one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Constitution (Part III).

NOTE

• The six Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural & Educational Rights (29–30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

question: A little child is a very picky eater and hates drinking milk and milk products. When he lost his baby tooth, permanent teeth took a very long time to come up in its place. What could be the probable reason behind this?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium Deficiency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As the child avoids milk and milk products (the richest sources of calcium), the delayed growth of teeth is most likely due to calcium deficiency. Calcium is essential for the formation of strong teeth and bones. (कैल्शियम की कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Calcium deficiency can cause weak bones, delayed tooth development, and osteoporosis.

• Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium; milk is often fortified with Vitamin D.

NOTE

• Rich sources of calcium: milk, cheese, curd, green leafy vegetables, and ragi. Calcium also helps in blood clotting and muscle contraction.

question: The 'Quit India Movement' was launched under the leadership of __________________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Quit India Movement" was launched on 8 August 1942 in Bombay under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, who gave the famous slogan "Do or Die". (भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन — महात्मा गांधी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The movement was launched after the failure of the Cripps Mission (1942).

• The All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India Resolution at its Bombay session; most top leaders were arrested immediately.

NOTE

• It is also called the August Kranti (August Revolution). Leaders like Aruna Asaf Ali, Ram Manohar Lohia and Jayaprakash Narayan kept the movement alive underground.

question: On May 23, 2023, who assumed the position of Chairperson at the Competition Commission of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravneet Kaur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 23 May 2023, Ravneet Kaur assumed office as the Chairperson of the Competition Commission of India (CCI). (रवनीत कौर — भारतीय प्रतिस्पर्धा आयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Competition Commission of India (CCI) was established under the Competition Act, 2002, and became fully functional in 2009.

• Its headquarters is in New Delhi. It works to promote fair competition and prevent monopolistic/anti-competitive practices.

NOTE

• The CCI protects consumer interests and ensures freedom of trade. It regulates mergers and acquisitions that may harm competition.

question: Which of the following Indian philosophical systems and its widely acknowledged proponents is INCORRECTLY paired?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaisheshika - Vyasa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pair "Vaisheshika - Vyasa" is incorrect. The Vaisheshika school was founded by Kanada (Rishi Kanada), not Vyasa. (वैशेषिक — कणाद द्वारा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The six orthodox (āstika) schools of Indian philosophy and their founders:

◦ Samkhya – Kapila; Yoga – Patanjali; Nyaya – Gautama (Gotama); Vaisheshika – Kanada; Purva Mimamsa – Jaimini; Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) – Vyasa (Badarayana).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

NOTE

• The Vaisheshika school is known for its atomic theory (Paramanu) — that all matter is made of tiny, indivisible atoms.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about public goods?

I. Rivalrous in consumption
II. Non-excludability
III. Positive marginal cost
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A public good has two defining features: it is non-rivalrous (one person's use does not reduce availability to others) and non-excludable (no one can be prevented from using it). So only statement II (Non-excludability) is true. (सार्वजनिक वस्तुएँ — गैर-अपवर्जनीय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Statement I is wrong — public goods are non-rivalrous, not rivalrous.

• Statement III is wrong — public goods generally have a zero marginal cost of providing to an additional user.

• Examples of public goods: national defence, street lighting, public parks, lighthouses.

NOTE

• Because of non-excludability, public goods suffer from the "free-rider problem", which is why they are usually provided by the government.

question: Which of the following folk dances of Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal region is on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chhau" — a semi-classical martial dance of the Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal region — was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010. (छऊ नृत्य — यूनेस्को)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chhau has three styles: Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

• It often depicts themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and local folklore, and uses masks (except Mayurbhanj).

NOTE

• Other Indian entries on UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list include Kutiyattam, Ramlila, Vedic chanting, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja in Kolkata, and Garba of Gujarat.

question: Where did the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023 take place in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023 were held in New Delhi, India (in March 2023). (आईबीए महिला विश्व मुक्केबाज़ी चैंपियनशिप 2023 — नई दिल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India won 4 gold medals at the event — through Nikhat Zareen, Lovlina Borgohain, Saweety Boora and Nitu Ghanghas.

• The championship is organised by the International Boxing Association (IBA).

NOTE

• Nikhat Zareen (born in Nizamabad, Telangana) is a two-time World Champion. Lovlina Borgohain won a bronze medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

question: The rifle (in the shooting sport) is single-loaded in _________-millimetre calibre (the inner diameter of a gun barrel), which is used across all events.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the shooting sport, the rifle is single-loaded in 5.6-millimetre calibre (equivalent to .22 inch), which is used across all rifle events. (5.6 मिमी कैलिबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Calibre" refers to the internal diameter of the gun barrel (or the diameter of the bullet).

• Olympic rifle and pistol shooting events use .22 calibre (5.6 mm) ammunition for events like the 10m air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, etc.

NOTE

• India's notable shooters include Abhinav Bindra (2008 Olympic gold, 10m air rifle), Gagan Narang, Manu Bhaker and Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore.

question: In Harappan civilisation, which material was NOT used in the construction of buildings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilisation did NOT use iron — iron was still unknown to them. They built with burnt/baked bricks, mud bricks, wood and gypsum mortar. (हड़प्पा सभ्यता — लोहे का प्रयोग नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Harappans were a Bronze Age civilisation; they used copper and bronze but not iron.

• They were famous for standardised burnt bricks in the ratio 4:2:1 and advanced town planning.

NOTE

• Iron technology came later, in the Vedic/Later Vedic period (around 1000 BCE), marking the start of the Iron Age in India.

question: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2013.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted by the Government of India in 2013. It provides subsidised food grains to about two-thirds of India's population. (राष्ट्रीय खाद्य सुरक्षा अधिनियम — 2013)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Under the NFSA, eligible households get 5 kg of food grain per person per month at subsidised prices (rice ₹3, wheat ₹2, coarse grains ₹1 per kg) through the Public Distribution System (PDS).

• It covers 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population.

NOTE

• The Act also provides maternity benefits and meals for pregnant/lactating women and children (through the ICDS and Mid-Day Meal schemes). It is also called the "Right to Food Act".

question: As of July 2023, how many products were notified under the 'One District, One Product' scheme as per the information provided by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 137.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2023, 137 products were notified under the "One District, One Product (ODOP)" scheme, as per the Ministry of Food Processing Industries. (एक ज़िला एक उत्पाद — 137 उत्पाद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The ODOP initiative promotes a specific product/craft from each district to boost local economy, exports and employment.

• It is linked with the PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme.

NOTE

• ODOP encourages "Vocal for Local" and helps in branding and value addition of traditional district-specific products (like Nagpur oranges, Bhagalpur silk, etc.).

question: Vibration or wave caused by the sudden movement of tectonic plates within the earth that can travel through and around the earth is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seismic Wave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Seismic wave" is the vibration/energy wave produced by the sudden movement of tectonic plates (as during an earthquake) that travels through and around the Earth. (भूकंपीय तरंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Seismic waves are of two main types: Body waves (P-waves and S-waves that travel through the Earth's interior) and Surface waves (that travel along the surface and cause most damage).

• P-waves (Primary) are the fastest; S-waves (Secondary) cannot pass through liquids.

NOTE

• Seismic waves are recorded by a seismograph; their magnitude is measured on the Richter scale and intensity on the Mercalli scale. The point of origin inside the Earth is the focus/hypocentre; the point directly above on the surface is the epicentre.

question: Which of the following agreements led Mahatma Gandhi to attend the Second Round Table Conference?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhi Irwin Pact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gandhi-Irwin Pact" (signed on 5 March 1931) led Mahatma Gandhi to attend the Second Round Table Conference (1931) in London, as a representative of the Congress. (गांधी-इरविन समझौता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under the pact, the government agreed to release political prisoners and Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.

• The Round Table Conferences (1930, 1931, 1932) were held to discuss constitutional reforms for India.

NOTE

• The Poona Pact (1932) was between Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar over separate electorates for the depressed classes. The Lucknow Pact (1916) was between the Congress and the Muslim League.

question: What is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems on Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunlight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sunlight (solar energy)" is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems on Earth. Green plants use sunlight in photosynthesis to produce food, forming the base of the food chain. (सूर्य का प्रकाश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In photosynthesis, plants convert carbon dioxide + water into glucose + oxygen using sunlight and chlorophyll.

• Plants are producers (autotrophs); the energy then flows to herbivores (primary consumers) and further along the food chain.

NOTE

• Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional (Sun → producers → consumers → decomposers). Only about 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level (the 10% law).

question: Who was the progenitor of the prolific Jaipur-Atrauli gharana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Alladiya Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Alladiya Khan was the founder (progenitor) of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana of Hindustani classical (vocal) music. (जयपुर-अतरौली घराना — उस्ताद अल्लादिया खान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A gharana is a school/lineage of music with a distinctive style, passed down through the guru-shishya parampara.

• Famous singers of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana include Kesarbai Kerkar and Mogubai Kurdikar.

NOTE

• Other well-known gharanas of Hindustani vocal music: Gwalior, Agra, Kirana, Patiala and Rampur-Sahaswan. Ustad Vilayat Khan and Ustad Ali Akbar Khan were instrumentalists (sitar and sarod respectively).

question: 0.25 g of an organic compound gave 0.20 g of CO2 after complete combustion. The percentage composition of carbon is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.82%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the combustion method for estimating carbon, the percentage of carbon is found using the formula:

◦ % of Carbon = (12 / 44) × (mass of CO₂ / mass of compound) × 100

• Here, mass of compound = 0.25 g and mass of CO₂ = 0.20 g.

◦ % C = (12 / 44) × (0.20 / 0.25) × 100

◦ % C = 0.2727 × 0.80 × 100 = 21.82%. (कार्बन का प्रतिशत — 21.82%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The factor 12/44 is used because in one molecule of CO₂ (molar mass 44), the mass of carbon is 12.

• Every 44 g of CO₂ produced corresponds to 12 g of carbon in the original compound.

NOTE

• This is based on Liebig's combustion method for the quantitative estimation of carbon and hydrogen in an organic compound. Similarly, % of Hydrogen = (2/18) × (mass of H₂O / mass of compound) × 100.
